topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: The Analogy: The Brain vs. The Library
sections.content: Introduce the concept that while Attention mechanisms act as a 'search engine' (looking at context), MLPs act as the 'long-term memory' (storing internal facts). Use a visual analogy where tokens are researchers and MLPs are encyclopedias.
sections.example: If the model reads 'The capital of France is...', the Attention mechanism looks at 'France', but the MLP layer provides the fact 'Paris'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Key-Value Projection
sections.content: Briefly explain that an MLP layer consists of two linear transformations with a non-linear activation (ReLU/GELU). Visualize this as a 'pattern matcher': Input vector matches a key, triggering an output vector.
sections.example: Visualize a grid of neurons lighting up like a constellation when the concept 'capital' + 'country' is detected.

sections.title: Mechanism: Key-Value Memory Networks
sections.content: Explain that MLPs function as a Key-Value memory. Each neuron can be seen as a template. The first layer acts as a 'Key' (detecting the query), and the second layer acts as a 'Value' (writing the factual information back into the token representation).
sections.example: A neuron's weight vector is tuned to identify 'Dog' and encodes the value 'Mammal' into the latent space.

sections.title: Visualizing Fact Retrieval
sections.content: Demonstrate the mathematical transformation: f(x) = W2 * σ(W1 * x + b1). Show how W1 matches the input pattern and W2 injects the fact. Animation: A signal flows through a narrow gate (bottleneck) and expands into a high-dimensional concept.
sections.example: Input: [Token 'Paris'] -> MLP processes it -> Output: [Vector representation of 'France' + 'Capital City']. The facts are distributed across the weights.

sections.title: Conclusion: Distributed Representation
sections.content: Summarize that facts are not stored in one 'cell', but are distributed across the weights of the MLP. This makes them 'synaptic memories' rather than a lookup table.
sections.example: If you erase a single neuron, the model still knows Paris is the capital, but if you change 5% of the weights, it might forget the link.
